author: nickbarnes
body:
There were four comments with the text "CR ocaml 5 domains," indicating things which had to be cleaned up, or at least checked, before multi-domain programs go live. This PR addresses all of them:

- `otherlibs/unix/signals.c` was basically the runtime4 version of this file. I've updated it to match (fairly well) the version from upstream. Semantically this just amounts to adding signals which are pending in the runtime to the list of signals returned by `caml_unix_sigpending()`. There are a couple of annoying hacks to make this still compile with runtime4, but it does.
- `runtime/extern.c` had a comment on `add_to_long_value` noting that it's multicore-unsafe. In fact this is fine because the function is only applied to fields of an array recently allocated by the same thread; no other core is going to race on it. I've augmented the comment and trivially refactored the function.
- `runtime4/caml/camlatomic.h` had a comment on some typedefs. This file (being `runtime4`) isn't a problem for runtime 5; the matching runtime 5 file already has the matching typedefs. I've removed the comment.
- `testsuite/tests/c-api/test_c_thread_has_lock_systhread.ml` had a comment remarking on the change in `caml_state` when using systhreads. This comment remains true; I have rewritten it to emphasize the distinction, and added a contrasting comment to the other (without `_systhread`) test.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/mdmasroorislam/skills-introduction-to-codeql/security/code-scanning/2](https://github.com/mdmasroorislam/skills-introduction-to-codeql/security/code-scanning/2)

To fix the issue, the SQL query should use parameterized queries instead of string concatenation. Parameterized queries ensure that user input is safely escaped and prevent SQL injection attacks. 

In this case, the `cursor.execute` method should be updated to use placeholders (`%s`) for the user-provided values, and the values should be passed as a separate argument to the `execute` method. This approach ensures that the database driver handles escaping and quoting of the input.

The same fix should also be applied to the query on line 16, as it suffers from the same vulnerability.

author: micbou
body:
Fixes #4843.

When running a program from the explorer context menu on Windows 11, its working directory is set to `C:\Windows\System32` because, looking at the code, the program seems to be run from `C:\Windows\System32\rundll32.dll`. This is an issue for programs that rely on the working directory to be its own directory. This is fixed by specifying the working directory to be the program's one when calling `ShellExecuteEx`.

I tested the changes by building a new version of Sandboxie and copying `SbieShellExt.dll` to an existing installation of Sandboxie. For some reason, I couldn't set the `Add 'Run Sandboxed' to the explorer context menu` option when directly running the new build.

- Expand types allowed in `.Object`
  - Originally, the Go template library limited the allowed types to structs and string maps. This pulls in an update that expands the allowed types.

author: toluolatundes
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces the foundational logic of the **Xanthic Herbarium Registry Protocol** written in Clarity. It supports decentralized specimen registration, scientific data validation, permissioned collaboration, and efficient querying of digitized herbarium records.

---

## What's Included

### ✅ New Clarity Contracts
- Core maps and data structures for herbarium entry and access permissions.

### 🆕 New Functionality
- `accession-new-specimen`, `register-herbarium-specimen`: Register new specimens with metadata.
- `amend-herbarium-record`: Update existing entries with new taxonomic information.
- `deaccession-specimen`: Securely remove entries.
- `visualize-herbarium-entry`, `generate-entry-visualization`: Generate structured views of specimen data.
- `query-herbarium-entry-basic`, `query-herbarium-minimal`, `extract-taxonomic-annotation`: Enable optimized and minimal data retrieval.
- `validate-accession-parameters`: Publicly verify accession validity prior to registration.

### 🔒 Security Enhancements
- Identity-based permission checks for amendment and deletion (`voucher-custodian` enforcement).
- Entry validation with comprehensive parameter assertions.

### 🛠 Refactors and Optimizations
- Functional redundancy between `accession-new-specimen` and `register-herbarium-specimen` is streamlined by offering alternative call structures.
- Use of `unwrap!`, `default-to`, and structured `let` bindings for safe access and gas efficiency.
- Efficient minimal and basic query interfaces reduce execution cost for large-scale lookups.

### 🐞 Bug Fixes
- Ensures missing or invalid entries are handled gracefully using consistent error codes (e.g., `MANIFEST_VIOLATION_NONEXISTENT_ENTRY`).
- Fixes possible omission of collaboration permission initialization by enforcing access entry creation at registration.

---

## Impact

This establishes a secure, performant, and extensible foundation for collaborative scientific registry of botanical specimens using Clarity smart contracts.

author: swalkinshaw
body:
Adds a `max_tokens` option to the parser which enforces a max tokens limit. The lexer will stop once the max tokens limit has been exceeded and return an error.

The parser has been changed to return a `ParseDetails` object which contains both the parsed AST and the `tokens_count`. This is exposed so that applications can log the tokens count regardless if the limit is exceeded or not and to determine a safe limit before enforcing it.

The `parse` function remains unchanged for compatibility and `parse_with_details` has to be explicitly called if you want the `token_count` returned. Regardless of the parse function used, token counting will still occur and an error returned if its exceeded.

I also explored using Logos' `extras` feature but it seemed even more complex because I'd have to implement a count callback on _every_ token. I don't think there's a concept of a generic callback and there was some other complexities too so I abandoned that approach. I definitely could have just missed something here though.

This mirrors the feature that was implemented in graphql-ruby: https://github.com/rmosolgo/graphql-ruby/pull/4929

There is a performance regression with this feature of course since we have to track the token count:

body:
## Description

Moving baseline initialization and cleanup from MC own Load and Unload calls to SO constructor and destructor for the Universal NRP. Second set is only executed every 15 minutes, which is 4 times per hour. First set is executed up to 24 times per hour. As the SO is not really unloaded during the first set, only the MC specific context being reset, we can prolong the life of our baseline instances to last 15 minutes each and with that, allow baselines such as ASB to not make that many package manager cache initialization calls.

author: thegoodduck
body:
Made it more resilient against Veyon 4.9.6 
This pull request refactors the `WinMain` function in `source.cpp` to introduce a custom window procedure (`WndProc`) and enhance window management features, including display affinity and rendering. The changes improve compatibility with Windows 10 and greater, optimize transparency handling, and add periodic updates to display affinity.

### Refactoring and Enhancements to Window Management:

* **Custom `WndProc` Implementation**:
  - Added a custom window procedure (`WndProc`) to handle `WM_TIMER` messages and periodically reapply display affinity using `SetWindowDisplayAffinity`.
  - Updated `WNDCLASS` to use `WndProc` instead of `DefWindowProc`.

* **Display Affinity Improvements**:
  - Introduced conditional logic to use `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE` for display affinity when running on Windows 10 or greater, falling back to `WDA_MONITOR` if unsupported.
  - Added a timer to periodically reapply display affinity every second.

* **Rendering Updates**:
  - Changed `SetLayeredWindowAttributes` to make the window black and opaque using `LWA_ALPHA`.
  - Filled the window with a black brush to ensure it is visually consistent across the screen.

### Code Cleanup:

* Removed `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` from the extended window styles to simplify transparency handling and avoid unintended behavior.

## 🐳 Docker Support Implementation

This PR adds comprehensive Docker support to PlotTwist with optimized, minimal footprint images suitable for both development and production environments.

### ✨ Features Added

#### Multi-Stage Docker Build
- **Development image**: ~200MB with debugging tools and auto-reload
- **Production image**: ~150MB optimized for runtime
- **Alpine Linux base** for security and minimal size

- Health checks for container monitoring

- **Makefile** with convenient commands (`make build`, `make run-dev`, etc.)

- **Auto-reload** in development mode

- **GitHub Actions workflow** for automated Docker builds
- **Multi-architecture support** preparation

body:
This PR modifies the `psycopg` sample to set `sslnegotiation=direct` as per #150.

It does this conditionally based on the underlying `libpq` version, since the same `psycopg` version can be used with multiple versions of `libpq`. I verified in the release notes [here](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.0/) that `sslnegotiation` has been available since the `17.0` release and was not added as a minor version bump.

I added a section to the `README.md` file which describes more about the TLS configuration, and calls out that direct TLS connections are a new feature and may not be supported by all driver versions. This section was already reviewed in #160, and will be added to all samples which support direct TLS connections.

# Issue #5 Resolution: Fit BarqCurve control points to curve

## Changes made to optspacecurve.py:

1.  Added `_fit_curve_to_control_points()` method using least squares + Bernstein matrix
    Uses JAX's `jnp.linalg.pinv()` for optimal performance with existing `beziertools` functions

2.  Enhanced `BarqCurve.initialize_parameters()` with 3 new optional parameters:
    *   `fit_target_curve`: function(t) -> `[x,y,z]` for curve fitting
    *   `fit_target_points`: array of target points for fitting
    *   `fit_n_samples`: number of samples for parameterization

3.  Maintains 100% backward compatibility - existing code works unchanged
    `barq_curve.initialize_parameters(seed=42)`  # Still works as before

4.  Enables informed initialization instead of random points, improving optimization performance
    `barq_curve.initialize_parameters(fit_target_curve=lambda t: [cos(t), sin(t), 0])`

body:
If a function `f : E × F → G` is continuously differentiable, then its partial derivatives along `E` and `F` are also continuous. The non-trivial converse implication holds when the partial derivatives are continuous on an open domain, and they can be added together to give the total derivative of `f`. See this [#mathlib4 > Partial derivatives @ 💬](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/287929-mathlib4/topic/Partial.20derivatives/near/520995477) and the containing thread for some discussion. The PR creates a new import (`Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Partial`), where other results about partial derivatives could go in the future.

author: knelsondev
body:
**Description:**

This PR addresses #6905 by expanding the documentation for the `--profile-execution` flag in the `nargo info` command. The previous documentation listed possible values but lacked context on the flag's purpose and utility.

**Enhancements:**

* **Detailed Explanation:** Added a comprehensive description of the `--profile-execution` flag, clarifying its role in profiling execution within the Brillig VM.
* **Use Case Illustration:** Highlighted scenarios where this flag is beneficial, such as analyzing performance bottlenecks in unconstrained functions with control flow constructs like loops and conditional statements.
* **Automatic Behavior:** Noted that enabling this flag automatically activates the Brillig VM, as execution profiling is pertinent to unconstrained code segments.

**Updated Documentation Snippet:**

```
* `--profile-execution` — Forces execution of binaries in the Brillig VM and profiles their execution. This is useful for analyzing the performance of unconstrained functions and identifying execution bottlenecks. When this flag is used, it automatically enables the Brillig VM, as execution profiling is only relevant for unconstrained code with control flow (e.g., loops and if statements).
```

**Impact:**

This enhancement aims to provide users with clearer guidance on utilizing the `--profile-execution` flag effectively, facilitating better performance analysis and optimization during development.

author: lwhsu
body:
The script now supports a more flexible snapshot_schedule format, allowing specific schedules for individual or comma-separated filesystems, alongside wildcard and global default schedules.

Key changes:
- Modified `snapshot_schedule` parsing to handle multiple, prioritized rules.
- Implemented precedence: exact match > comma-separated list > specific wildcard > global wildcard.
- Longer wildcard patterns take precedence over shorter ones.
- Reused and adapted existing logic for time parsing and snapshot execution.
- Added extensive scenario-based checks (mocked environment) to verify functionality.

This addresses the requirement to allow configurations like: `snapshot_schedule="/j/jails/*:2:8:24 /j/jails/ftpsync-master,/j/jails/cgit:0:0:0 /j/jails/xyz:1:7:16"`

Fixes https://github.com/ray-project/kuberay-helm/issues/63 

For example if you now define the topologySpreadConstraint like so

```
worker:
  topologySpreadConstraints:
    - maxSkew: 1
      topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
      whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
      labelSelector:
        matchLabels:
          service: ray-worker
```

this outputs the correct manifest with the TSC.

```
  workerGroupSpecs:
  - rayStartParams:
      {}
    replicas: 1
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 3
    numOfHosts: 1
    groupName: workergroup
    template:
      spec:
        imagePullSecrets:
          []
        containers:
          - 
            volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /tmp/ray
              name: log-volume
            name: ray-worker
            image: rayproject/ray:2.41.0
            imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
            resources:
              limits:
                cpu: "1"
                memory: 1G
              requests:
                cpu: "1"
                memory: 1G
            securityContext:
              {}
        
        volumes:
          - emptyDir: {}
            name: log-volume
        topologySpreadConstraints:
          - labelSelector:
              matchLabels:
                service: ray-worker
            maxSkew: 1
            topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
            whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
```

Also fixes TSC for head node and additional worker groups as well.

author: cheffromspace
body:
## Summary
Comprehensive Docker CI/CD optimization featuring:
- ✅ Multi-stage builds for efficient caching and smaller images
- ✅ Container-based test execution for consistency
- ✅ Enhanced caching strategies with GitHub Actions cache
- ✅ Simplified workflow that works reliably
- ✅ All CI checks passing

This PR is a squashed version of #129 with all commits combined into a single, clean commit.

## Key Changes

### 1. Multi-Stage Dockerfile
```dockerfile
# Build stage - TypeScript compilation
FROM node:24-slim AS builder

# Test stage - includes dev dependencies
FROM node:24-slim AS test

# Production dependencies only
FROM node:24-slim AS prod-deps

# Final minimal production image
FROM node:24-slim AS production
```

### 2. Container-Based Testing
- Tests run inside Docker containers for consistency
- New `docker-compose.test.yml` for orchestrating test services
- Coverage reports exported from containers

### 3. Simplified Workflow
- Removed complex matrix strategy that was causing issues
- Direct docker build commands for PR testing
- Multi-platform builds only for main branch pushes
- Separate claudecode build to avoid complexity

### 4. Caching Strategy
- GitHub Actions cache (GHA) for all builds
- Optimized layer ordering for better cache hits
- Separate caches for test and production builds

## Results

### Before
- Single-stage Dockerfile
- Tests run on host system
- No container-based testing
- Basic caching

### After
- Multi-stage builds with separate test/production stages
- Tests run in containers
- Smaller production images (no dev dependencies)
- Improved build caching
- All CI checks passing ✅

## Testing
```bash
# Local testing with Docker
docker build --target test -t claude-hub:test .
docker run --rm claude-hub:test npm test

# Or using docker-compose
docker-compose -f docker-compose.test.yml run test
```

## Documentation
Added comprehensive guide at `docs/docker-optimization.md` covering:
- Multi-stage build benefits
- Caching strategies
- Container-based testing
- Performance tips

## Migration Notes
- **Non-root user**: Production container now runs as `claudeuser` (not root)
- No breaking changes for existing workflows
- Backward compatible with current Docker images
- Ready to add self-hosted runners in the future

## Related PRs
- Supersedes #129 (squashed version)

<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.20.3
   ```
   Java
  * Refactoring java full runtime to reuse sub-message builders and prepare to
    migrate parsing logic from parse constructor to builder.
  * Move proto wireformat parsing functionality from the private "parsing
    constructor" to the Builder class.
  * Change the Lite runtime to prefer merging from the wireformat into mutable
    messages rather than building up a new immutable object before merging. This
    way results in fewer allocations and copy operations.
  * Make message-type extensions merge from wire-format instead of building up
    instances and merging afterwards. This has much better performance.
  * Fix TextFormat parser to build up recurring (but supposedly not repeated)
    sub-messages directly from text rather than building a new sub-message and
    merging the fully formed message into the existing field.
  * This release addresses a [Security Advisory for Java users](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-h4h5-3hr4-j3g2)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.20.2
   ```
   C++
* Reduce memory consumption of MessageSet parsing
* This release addresses a [Security Advisory for C++ and Python users](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-8gq9-2x98-w8hf)
   ```

  * Fix conversion of singleton classes in Ruby (9342)

   Java
  * Revert "Standardize on Array copyOf" (9400)

  * Add orNull extensions for optional message fields.

   Python
  * Dropped support for Python < 3.7 (9480)
  * Protoc is now able to generate python stubs (.pyi) with --pyi_out
  * Pin multibuild scripts to get manylinux1 wheels back (9216)
  * Fix type annotations of some Duration and Timestamp methods.
  * Repeated field containers are now generic in field types and could be used
    in type annotations.
  *[Breaking change] Protobuf python generated codes are simplified. Descriptors and message
    classes' definitions are now dynamic created in internal/builder.py.
    Insertion Points for messages classes are discarded.
  * has_presence is added for FieldDescriptor in python

  * Fix the deepcopy bug caused by not copying message_listener.

  * Adds client_streaming and server_streaming fields to MethodDescriptor.

body:
## About The Pull Request

This PR ports (and actually makes work?) Vanderlin's Thieves Cant changes. Namely:

- It gives Thieves Cant to the appropriate classes, such as Thieves, the Bathmaster, the Spymaster Hand, Ex-Spy Veteran, Thug Towner, and such.
- Makes Thieves Cant into a SIGNLANG and adds SIGNLANG handling. It can be "spoken" without a tongue, cannot be "heard" through walls or Z-levels, or be picked up by SCOMs, because it is signed. Those who don't know Thieves Cant will instead see a little random emote being played, like so:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddf4ee57-651f-4f68-b23a-b6f9127915f9)![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/948406b2-9983-45a1-8e1e-acbe6e3d9a4d)
**THIS PROBABLY NEEDS A LOT MORE TESTING. I'VE DONE ALL THE TESTING I COULD.**

- Adds Thieves Engravings. These are a type of tracks that those who know thieves' cant can etch onto walls by using a small, sharp object (same check as carving things onto a sign). They're easier to notice than other tracks or clues, but only those with knowledge of the cant can understand them.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c500645-7ad2-440a-893b-cfc4708cce34)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77492069-cdd0-4f83-8915-9bbae11faab0)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0512443-9fe3-400f-b056-cc2ad4441c72)

TO BE CONSIDERED:
- Granting Thieves Cant through a virtue?
- Removing engravings?
- Allowing rocky surfaces/trees to also be engraved?
- Giving Xylix worshipers another trait, as a treat?

<!-- Describe your pull request. Avoid text walls, use concise bullet points for easier readability. Document every change, or this can delay review and even discourage maintainers from merging your PR. -->

## Testing Evidence

See the images above.

<!-- It's mandatory to test your PR. Provide images, clips or description of how you tested your changes where possible. -->

## Why It's Good For The Game

The main issue of playing thief characters is that, naturally, you tend to work alone. This gives thieves several tools to communicate between themselves almost secretly.

Thieves' Cant also stops being a way to confirm someone as a Xylix follower as it is no longer exclusive to them. This also means that Xylixians speaking the Cant out in the open can be misidentified as thieves!

## Summary
- Added support for parsing the new JSONL format from `~/.claude/projects/` directories
- Implemented dynamic model name matching to handle version variations
- Enhanced cost analysis with actual API usage data

## Changes
1. **New JSONL Parser** (`bin/jsonl-parser.js`)
   - Reads JSONL files from project directories
   - Extracts token usage, costs, and duration from each API call
   - Aggregates data by project and model

2. **Updated Stats Generation**
   - Modified `stats` and `dashboard` commands to use JSONL data
   - Falls back to legacy `.claude.json` format if no JSONL data exists
   - Shows actual costs from `costUSD` field instead of estimates

3. **Dynamic Model Matching**
   - Replaced hardcoded model names with pattern matching
   - Handles variations like `claude-opus-4-20250514` and `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`
   - Displays request counts alongside costs for each model

## Test Results
The updated tool successfully:
- Found 8,804 API calls across 13 projects
- Calculated total actual cost of $1,489.72
- Properly displayed both Opus ($1,449.28) and Sonnet ($53.01) usage
- Demonstrated 86.7% savings compared to API pricing

## Summary
- Added support for parsing the new JSONL format from `~/.claude/projects/` directories
- Implemented dynamic model name matching to handle version variations
- Enhanced cost analysis with actual API usage data

## Changes
1. **New JSONL Parser** (`bin/jsonl-parser.js`)
   - Reads JSONL files from project directories
   - Extracts token usage, costs, and duration from each API call
   - Aggregates data by project and model

2. **Updated Stats Generation**
   - Modified `stats` and `dashboard` commands to use JSONL data
   - Falls back to legacy `.claude.json` format if no JSONL data exists
   - Shows actual costs from `costUSD` field instead of estimates

3. **Dynamic Model Matching**
   - Replaced hardcoded model names with pattern matching
   - Handles variations like `claude-opus-4-20250514` and `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`
   - Displays request counts alongside costs for each model

## Test Results
The updated tool successfully:
- Found 8,804 API calls across 13 projects
- Calculated total actual cost of $1,489.72
- Properly displayed both Opus ($1,449.28) and Sonnet ($53.01) usage

This commit introduces a series of enhancements to the trading bot:

Performance:
- Optimized chart rendering in `chart_manager.py` by reducing full axis clears and managing artists directly.
- Optimized `data_manager.py`:
    - Implemented delta updates for k-line data fetching, reducing API load.
    - Vectorized the 'touches' calculation in `calculate_density_zones`.
    - Improved efficiency of other calculations within `calculate_density_zones`.
- Improved UI responsiveness in `trading_bot.py` by:
    - Moving ML feature preparation and prediction to separate threads.
    - Implementing batched updates for the logging widget.

Stability & Bug Fixes:
- Enhanced error handling in data fetching (`data_manager.py`), WebSocket communication, and threaded operations (`trading_bot.py`).
- Added more detailed logging across modules for better diagnostics.
- Addressed potential `NameError` in `calculate_density_zones`.
- Made WebSocket connection management more robust.

Testing:
- Introduced unit tests for `data_manager.py`, covering k-line data handling and density zone calculation logic.
- Introduced unit tests for `ml_manager.py`, covering feature preparation and prediction method calls.

These changes aim to make the bot more performant, stable, and maintainable.

author: mdeeks
body:
The API Handler and AI Proxy can now be assigned reserved concurrency with these two vars:
* `api_handler_reserved_concurrent_executions`
* `ai_proxy_reserved_concurrent_executions`

AWS has an account-wide regional limit on the maximum concurrency for **all** Lambdas, and not just Braintrust's lambdas. Typically this defaults to 1000. 

By default, these reserved concurrency params are set to unlimited (`-1`). That means a large sudden spike in traffic to the API Handler can cause other Lambdas in your account to get throttled and fail to execute.

Setting these values will allow you to reserve and constraint the maximum concurrency for the Braintrust lambdas. Note that setting these values takes away from your account-wide AWS limit and holds it in reserve for the Lambda. In other words, if you set both of these to 100, then you will only have 800 remaining concurrency for your other Lambdas in your account.

If you host Braintrust in a shared AWS account **it is highly recommended you set these**. For small deployments, 10 is fine. For larger deployments 100-1000 is likely needed. You will need to inspect Cloudwatch graphs to confirm historical usage.

author: j9liu
body:
This PR checks for the `3DTILES_content_voxels` extension on the root tile's content. If present, it passes the value all the way to through to the `TilesetContentManager`.

It feels awkward to pass it around like this, but it's not like there's an explicit `Content` instance on the root tile that the extension can keep living on. This felt like the best way to bubble it up so we can query if it exists through the `Tileset`. There might be a nicer way to handle this that I'm not aware of. 🤔

body:
### TLDR
Add keyboard shortcuts to jump to first/last slides and fix null pointer crashes.

## Change Summary

#### Added Features:
1. **New Navigation Methods in `slide.go`**:
   - `First()`: Navigate to the first slide in the presentation chain
   - `Last()`: Navigate to the last slide in the presentation chain

2. **New Key Bindings in `tui.go`**:
   - `Top`: Jump to first slide using `home`, `shift+up`, or `0` keys
   - `Bottom`: Jump to last slide using `end`, `shift+down`, or `$` keys

#### Code Changes:
1. **In `slide.go`**:
   - Added null pointer safety checks in `view()` method to prevent crashes during transitions
   - Added panic handling for backwards transitions at the last slide
   - Fixed potential null pointer dereference when `s.Prev` is nil during forward transitions
   - Removed extra blank line for cleaner formatting

2. **In `tui.go`**:
   - Extended `keyMap` struct with `Top` and `Bottom` key bindings
   - Added keyboard shortcuts mapping for quick navigation
   - Implemented navigation logic in `Update()` method using new slide methods

#### Documentation Updates:
1. **In `tui.go`**:
   - Updated help text to include new navigation shortcuts

This PR updates [protobuf](https://pypi.org/project/protobuf) from **3.14.0** to **6.31.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 3.20.3
   ```
   Java
  * Refactoring java full runtime to reuse sub-message builders and prepare to
    migrate parsing logic from parse constructor to builder.
  * Move proto wireformat parsing functionality from the private "parsing
    constructor" to the Builder class.
  * Change the Lite runtime to prefer merging from the wireformat into mutable
    messages rather than building up a new immutable object before merging. This
    way results in fewer allocations and copy operations.
  * Make message-type extensions merge from wire-format instead of building up
    instances and merging afterwards. This has much better performance.
  * Fix TextFormat parser to build up recurring (but supposedly not repeated)
    sub-messages directly from text rather than building a new sub-message and
    merging the fully formed message into the existing field.
  * This release addresses a [Security Advisory for Java users](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-h4h5-3hr4-j3g2)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 3.20.2
   ```
   C++
* Reduce memory consumption of MessageSet parsing
* This release addresses a [Security Advisory for C++ and Python users](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/security/advisories/GHSA-8gq9-2x98-w8hf)
   ```

   ```
   PHP
  * Fix building packaged PHP extension (9727)

  Ruby

 Other

   2022-03-25 version 3.20.0 (C++/Java/Python/PHP/Objective-C/C/Ruby/JavaScript)

  Ruby
  * Dropped Ruby 2.3 and 2.4 support for CI and releases. (9311)
  * Added Ruby 3.1 support for CI and releases (9566).
  * Message.decode/encode: Add recursion_limit option (9218/9486)
  * Allocate with xrealloc()/xfree() so message allocation is visible to the
    Ruby GC.  In certain tests this leads to much lower memory usage due to more
    frequent GC runs (9586).
  * Fix conversion of singleton classes in Ruby (9342)
  * Suppress warning for intentional circular require (9556)
  * JSON will now output shorter strings for double and float fields when possible
    without losing precision.
  * Encoding and decoding of binary format will now work properly on big-endian
    systems.
  * UTF-8 verification was fixed to properly reject surrogate code points.
  * Unknown enums for proto2 protos now properly implement proto2's behavior of
    putting such values in unknown fields.

   Java
  * Revert "Standardize on Array copyOf" (9400)
  * Resolve more java field accessor name conflicts (8198)
  * Don't support map fields in DynamicMessage.Builder.{getFieldBuilder,getRepeatedFieldBuilder}
  * Fix parseFrom to only throw InvalidProtocolBufferException
  * InvalidProtocolBufferException now allows arbitrary wrapped Exception types.
  * Fix bug in `FieldSet.Builder.mergeFrom`
  * Flush CodedOutputStream also flushes underlying OutputStream
  * When oneof case is the same and the field type is Message, merge the
    subfield. (previously it was replaced.)’
  * Add CheckReturnValue to some protobuf types
  * Report original exceptions when parsing JSON
  * Add more info to deprecated javadoc for set/get/has methods
  * Fix initialization bug in doc comment line numbers
  * Fix comments for message set wire format.

   Kotlin
  * Add test scope to kotlin-test for protobuf-kotlin-lite (9518)
  * Add orNull extensions for optional message fields.
  * Add orNull extensions to all proto3 message fields.

   Python
  * Dropped support for Python < 3.7 (9480)
  * Protoc is now able to generate python stubs (.pyi) with --pyi_out
  * Pin multibuild scripts to get manylinux1 wheels back (9216)
  * Fix type annotations of some Duration and Timestamp methods.
  * Repeated field containers are now generic in field types and could be used
    in type annotations.
  *[Breaking change] Protobuf python generated codes are simplified. Descriptors and message
    classes' definitions are now dynamic created in internal/builder.py.
    Insertion Points for messages classes are discarded.
  * has_presence is added for FieldDescriptor in python
  * Loosen indexing type requirements to allow valid __index__() implementations
    rather than only PyLongObjects.
  * Fix the deepcopy bug caused by not copying message_listener.
  * Added python JSON parse recursion limit (default 100)
  * Path info is added for python JSON parse errors
  * Pure python repeated scalar fields will not able to pickle. Convert to list
    first.
  * Timestamp.ToDatetime() now accepts an optional tzinfo parameter. If
    specified, the function returns a timezone-aware datetime in the given time
    zone. If omitted or None, the function returns a timezone-naive UTC datetime
    (as previously).
  * Adds client_streaming and server_streaming fields to MethodDescriptor.
  * Add "ensure_ascii" parameter to json_format.MessageToJson. This allows smaller
    JSON serializations with UTF-8 or other non-ASCII encodings.
  * Added experimental support for directly assigning numpy scalars and array.
  * Improve the calculation of public_dependencies in DescriptorPool.
  * [Breaking Change] Disallow setting fields to numpy singleton arrays or repeated fields to numpy
    multi-dimensional arrays. Numpy arrays should be indexed or flattened explicitly before assignment.

  * Fixed bugs in operators for RepeatedPtrIterator
  * Assert a maximum map alignment for allocated values
  * Fix proto1 group extension protodb parsing error

  * Fix unreferenced parameter for MSVC builds

  * Add option to use external GTest in CMake (8736)
  * CMake: Set correct sonames for libprotobuf-lite.so and libprotoc.so (8635) (9529)

  * CMake: Use linker version scripts (9545)
  * Manually *struct Cord fields to work better with arenas.
  * Manually destruct map fields.
  * Generate narrower code
  * Fix https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf/issues/9378 by removing
    shadowed _cached_size_ field
  * Remove GetPointer() and explicit nullptr defaults.
  * Add proto_h flag for speeding up large builds

author: copilot
body:
This PR updates the LLM implementation to use `o4-mini` as the default model and introduces support for Azure OpenAI environment variables while maintaining full backward compatibility.

## Changes Made

### 🔧 Core Updates
- **Default Model**: Changed from `gpt-4` to `o4-mini` 
- **Environment Variables**: Added support for new Azure OpenAI environment variables:
  - `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` - Azure OpenAI endpoint URL (preferred)
  - `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` - Azure OpenAI API key (preferred)
  - Maintains fallback to existing `OPENAI_URL` and `OPENAI_API_KEY` for backward compatibility

### 📚 Documentation
- Updated README.md with clear examples of the new environment variables
- Added migration guidance showing both new and legacy variable usage

### 🧹 Code Quality
- Removed unused import (`github.com/sashabaranov/go-openai`)
- Improved error messages to reference the preferred environment variables

## Example Usage

### New (Recommended)
```bash
export AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://your-resource.openai.azure.com
export AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY=your-azure-openai-api-key-here
export OPENAI_MODEL=o4-mini
```

### Legacy (Still Supported)
```bash
export OPENAI_URL=https://apiendpoint.openai.azure.com
export OPENAI_API_KEY=your-openai-api-key-here
export OPENAI_MODEL=o4-mini
```

## Backward Compatibility

The implementation prioritizes new Azure OpenAI environment variables while gracefully falling back to existing ones, ensuring:
- ✅ No breaking changes for current users
- ✅ All existing tests continue to pass
- ✅ Seamless transition path to new variables

## Testing

- All existing tests pass without modification
- Code builds successfully without errors
- Manual verification of environment variable fallback logic

Fixes #21.

author: nomike
body:
Currently the CMake code in regards to the HidAPI library is weird.

There is a flag "USE_HIDAPI", but if it's set to "ON" and HidAPI is not found, it will be ignored (similar to how `USE_PYTHON` is set to "OFF" if the requirement "Nettle" is not found (See #5897)).

If the flag "ALLOW_BUNDLED_HIDAPI" is set to "ON", the bundled HidAPI is used, but only if HidAPI is not found in the system using `find_package` first.
And despite the description of that flag stating that this is only supported on Windows, this would still happen on non-Windows platforms.

This pull request aims to clean this up.
The flag "ALLOW_BUNDLED_HIDAPI" is replaced with "USE_BUNDLED_HIDAPI". When it is set to "ON", bundled HidAPI is used, regardless of whether it is available system wide.
As this is only supported on Windows, a fatal error is thrown if that flag is set to true on non-windows platforms.

If the flag is not set, the system wide HidAPI library is looked up and if there is none with the required minimum version, the build will fail, notifying the user, so they can either address this or take the decision to set "USE_HIDAPI" to "OFF".

I don't know why bundled HidAPI is only supported on Winwodws (a comment explaining that, ideally with a link to some ticket or article going into more detail would be nice), so maybe a WARNING would be sufficient in case someone tries to use "ALLOW_BUNDLED_HIDAPI" on a non Windows platform.

author: chexo7
body:
This commit refines the cash flow calculation logic in `app.js` to ensure accurate assignment of incomes, expenses, and reimbursements to weekly or monthly periods.

Key changes:

1.  **New Date Helper Functions:**
    *   `getPeriodStartDate(date, periodicity)`: Determines the precise start date (Monday for weekly, 1st for monthly) of a period.
    *   `getPeriodEndDate(date, periodicity)`: Determines the precise end date (Sunday for weekly, last day for monthly) of a period.
    *   These functions operate in UTC.

2.  **Refactored `calculateCashFlowData`:**
    *   Uses the new helper functions for accurate period boundary (`p_start`, `p_end`) determination.
    *   Replaced approximate calculations (e.g., `* 52/12`) with precise, date-based logic for all transaction frequencies ("Único", "Mensual", "Semanal", "Bi-semanal").
    *   Correctly counts occurrences of weekly/bi-weekly items within monthly periods.
    *   Ensures monthly items are accurately assigned to specific weeks if the payment day falls within that week during weekly analysis.
    *   Applied the same precision to reimbursement calculations.

3.  **Bug Fix in Date Logic:**
    *   During testing, I identified a bug in the existing `getMondayOfWeek` helper function that affected calculations around year boundaries for ISO weeks. I have corrected this function.

4.  **Unit Testing:**
    *   I created unit tests for the new date helpers and the core financial event processing logic within `calculateCashFlowData`, covering various scenarios, frequencies, periodicities, and boundary conditions. All tests passed after the aforementioned bug fix.

These changes ensure that the cash flow projection is more robust, consistent, and accurate, regardless of the chosen analysis periodicity (weekly or monthly) and the frequency of individual financial items.

body:
<!-- Please refer to our contributing documentation for any questions on submitting a pull request, or let us know here if you need any help: https://github.com/stenciljs/core/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Currently, Stencil has duplicate shadow root creation logic scattered across multiple runtime files (`bootstrap-lazy.ts`, `bootstrap-custom-element.ts`, and `proxy-host-element.ts`). Each location manually calls `attachShadow()` with conditional logic for `delegatesFocus` support.

Additionally, there is no mechanism to apply global styles to shadow DOM components. While Stencil supports global styles for non-shadow components, shadow DOM components remain isolated from these styles, creating inconsistencies in styling across component types.

The existing global styles infrastructure exists but is only used for generating output files - it's not integrated into the runtime for shadow DOM components.

fixes #1967

## What is the new behavior?
<!-- Please describe the behavior or changes that are being added by this PR. -->

This PR introduces comprehensive global styles support for shadow DOM components by:

### 🎨 **Global Styles Integration**
- **Automatic Application**: Global styles are now automatically applied to all shadow DOM components via `adoptedStyleSheets`
- **Performance Optimized**: Uses constructable stylesheets for efficient style sharing across shadow roots
- **Build-time Integration**: Global styles are compiled and bundled at build time, eliminating runtime style processing

### 🔧 **Code Consolidation** 
- **Unified Shadow Root Creation**: Created a new `createShadowRoot()` utility function in `src/utils/shadow-root.ts`
- **DRY Principle**: Eliminated duplicate shadow root creation code across three runtime files
- **Consistent Behavior**: Ensures all shadow roots are created with the same logic and global styles applied

### 🏗️ **Build System Enhancements**
- **@app-globals Module**: Extended the module system to export `globalStyles` alongside existing `globalScripts`
- **Cross-Platform Support**: Updated esbuild configurations for client, hydrate, and testing platforms to handle the new module
- **Type Safety**: Updated TypeScript declarations to reflect that `BuildCtx.stylesPromise` now returns the compiled styles string

### 📦 **Bundle Generation**
- **App Data Plugin**: Enhanced to include global styles in the generated bundles
- **Conditional Building**: Global styles are only included when `config.globalStyle` is defined
- **JSON Serialization**: Styles are properly serialized and embedded in the bundle for runtime access

## Technical Implementation Details

### New Utility Function
```typescript
export function createShadowRoot(this: HTMLElement, cmpMeta: d.ComponentRuntimeMeta) {
  const shadowRoot = BUILD.shadowDelegatesFocus
    ? this.attachShadow({
        mode: 'open',
        delegatesFocus: !!(cmpMeta.$flags$ & CMP_FLAGS.shadowDelegatesFocus),
      })
    : this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });

  const sheet = new CSSStyleSheet();
  sheet.replaceSync(globalStyles);
  shadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets.push(sheet);
}
```

### Build Process Integration
- Global styles are processed during the style build phase
- The compiled CSS is made available through the `@app-globals` module
- Build configurations across all platforms now include the necessary external alias for `@app-globals`

## Does this introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

<!-- If this introduces a breaking change, please describe the impact and migration path for existing applications below. -->

This is a purely additive feature that enhances existing functionality without breaking current behavior:

- **Backward Compatible**: Existing shadow DOM components continue to work exactly as before
- **Automatic Enhancement**: Global styles are automatically applied without requiring code changes
- **Performance Improvement**: The code consolidation actually improves performance by reducing bundle size
- **Optional Feature**: Global styles are only applied when `globalStyle` is configured in the Stencil config

author: mitchellh
body:
This brings the behavior of mode 47, 1047, and 1049 much closer to xterm's behavior. I found that our prior implementation had many deficiencies.

For example, we weren't properly copying the cursor state back to the primary screen from the alternate screen for modes 47 and 1047. And we weren't saving/restoring cursor state unconditionally for mode 1049 even if we were already in the alternate screen.

I also found that we were dangling hyperlink state on the primary screen when we switched to alternate. xterm doesn't support hyperlinks but we did the opposite behavior for going from alternate to primary. So one way or the other its a bug. I'm worried this one could've maybe led to memory corruption under the right circumstances but I wasn't able to prove it.

These are weird, edgy behaviors that I don't think anyone expected (evidence by there being no bug reports about them), but they are bugs nontheless.

Many tests added.

(Btw: this flew under the radar of our "xterm audit" because that only included sequences and not modes. I noted this in the audit issue itself but just an FYI.)
